what_it_does: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) is an alternative computing style where every object — a medical reading, a spoken word — is represented as an extremely long string of numbers (a hypervector) and classification is done by comparing how similar two hypervectors are. HDC naturally supports early stopping: you can look at partial results and potentially answer before reading all the data, saving energy. The problem is that previous early-stopping rules were guesses with no mathematical guarantees — they might quit too soon and give a wrong answer, or quit too late and waste computation. This paper replaces the guesswork with formal hypothesis testing, a branch of statistics that lets you quantify how confident you are in a conclusion. The method stops inference only when a statistical test can prove, within a user-chosen confidence threshold, that one class has beaten all others — giving a provable upper bound on how much accuracy is lost while minimizing wasted work.
